title: 10-11. I NEVER EXPECTED TO SEE YOUR FACE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Now Israel's eyes were failing because of old age, and he could hardly see. So Joseph brought his sons close to him, and his father kissed them and embraced them. Israel said to Joseph, 'I never expected to see your face again, and now God has allowed me to see your children too.'" — Gen 48:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"I never expected to see your face again."

For over twenty years Jacob had lived with a settled certainty: Joseph was dead. He had grieved it, wept over it, refused to be comforted about it. That was simply how his story had gone, and there was no reason to imagine otherwise.

And now his blind old hands are on the faces of Joseph's children.

God gave him more than he ever dared hope for. Not just the son back, but grandchildren he did not know existed.

Be careful here — this is not a promise that everything you have grieved will be restored in this life. Jacob had already buried Rachel and would never see her again. Some losses stay lost on this side. But it does tell us that God is often doing more than we can see, and that our expectations are frequently too small for Him.

Paul prayed to God as the one able to do immeasurably more than all we ask or imagine (Eph 3:20). Jacob would have said Amen to that with tears running down his face.

Do not let your grief shrink your view of what God can do.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where have your expectations of God become smaller than He is?
2. What has God given you that you never expected?
3. Is there a situation you have written off as finished?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, my expectations of You are often too small. Thank You for the good You have given me that I never dared to hope for. Enlarge my faith in what You are able to do. Amen.
